advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Avoid the second full _load_ticket_events walk in select_from_corpus (reuse build_corpus's parse or fold finding extraction into the corpus rows).
advisory.finding: select_from_corpus walks and parses the entire tickets tracker git history twice: build_corpus -> _rows_for_store -> _load_ticket_events(tracker), then _review_findings(tracker) calls corpus._load_ticket_events(tracker) again to re-extract findings. On a large committed corpus this doubles the git-object walk and JSON parse cost.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Note/guard that the default select_from_corpus reader mutates the global REBAR_TRACKER_DIR and is not concurrency-safe.
evidence: docstring claims 'Pure git + local hashing: no model call, no network.' at fixture_selection.py:441-442
advisory.finding: The default ticket-state reader used by select_from_corpus (_read_ticket_state_via_env_override) mutates the process-global os.environ['REBAR_TRACKER_DIR'] with save/restore around each show_ticket call, invoked in the enrichment loop. This global mutation is not safe under concurrent/parallel selector runs sharing the process and undermines the 'pure git + local hashing, deterministic' framing in the docstring.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop the unused criterion_id parameter from _eligible_reviews (or document why it is retained).
evidence: `def _eligible_reviews(reviews: list[dict[str, Any]], criterion_id: str, rubric_ts: int)` at fixture_selection.py:161-163
body references only `r["review_event_ts"]` and `rubric_ts`, never `criterion_id`, at fixture_selection.py:164-167
advisory.finding: _eligible_reviews accepts a criterion_id parameter it never uses (the filter is purely on review_event_ts > rubric_ts), which is misleading given other helpers with the same signature do filter by criterion.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a select_candidates test with 2+ criteria_ids asserting rows are grouped per criterion in criteria_ids order.
evidence: Every select_candidates call in the held-out suite uses `criteria_ids=[C]` (single element) — see lines 54,109,123,143,262,282,317,345,364,384,407,422
Docstring contract (fixture_selection.py select_candidates): "Rows are returned already ordered: grouped per criterion (in ``criteria_ids`` order)"
ABSENCE: no test passes two or more criteria to assert the grouping/ordering across criteria
fixture_selection.py _no_fire_rows: `"escaped_defect": any(_escaped(review) for review in silent),`
no-fire tests (test_no_fire_admitted_only_when_routed_and_uncited, test_single_criterion_emits_both...) build routed_silent reviews with no ticket_state, so escaped_defect is always False
ABSENCE: no test asserts escaped_defect True on a no_fire candidate
advisory.finding: select_candidates' documented per-criterion grouping and ordering across multiple criteria_ids is never exercised — every test passes a single-element criteria_ids list, so a regression that mis-groups or mis-orders rows for a multi-criterion request (e.g. interleaving criteria, or emitting a criterion's rows out of criteria_ids order) would not be caught.
merged_from: The no_fire candidate's escaped_defect field is computed from the silent reviews (fixture_selection.py:301) but is never asserted True — all no-fire tests use non-escaped reviews, so a regression zeroing escaped_defect on the no_fire path would pass.
scenarios: A refactor of the per-criterion loop in select_candidates that reorders or interleaves rows across criteria

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting last_rubric_commit_ts returns None when base_ref is absent / repo_root is not a git repo.
evidence: Only one direct call: `got = last_rubric_commit_ts(C, repo_root=str(tmp_path), base_ref="HEAD")` asserting `got == expected` (line 96)

fixture_selection.py last_rubric_commit_ts: `except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError, FileNotFoundError, PromptNotFound): return None` and `if not text: return None` and the `except ValueError: return None` branches
ABSENCE: no test asserts last_rubric_commit_ts returns None for a missing base_ref / non-git repo_root / empty git output
advisory.finding: last_rubric_commit_ts' fail-closed None branches (git CalledProcessError/OSError, empty stdout, non-int output) are never directly asserted; only its happy path (returns a real commit ts) is covered, despite the docstring emphasizing it 'Never raises' and returns None on absent base_ref / git err.
scenarios: Shallow clone or differently-named remote where base_ref is absent
